question: What are the three primary components evaluated when analyzing the causes of abnormal labour progression?

options.A: Pelvis, Partograph, Pushing
options.B: Power, Passenger, Passage
options.C: Perineum, Protein, Position
options.D: Placenta, Pressure, Pulse

explanation: The classic obstetric triad governing labour progress consists of the power of contractions, the passenger, and the birth passage. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T010#GNS226_U4_T010_h2)

question: A patient with strong, frequent uterine contractions fails to dilate further because the fetal head is too large for the pelvis. Which element of labour is primarily affected here?

options.A: Power
options.B: Passenger
options.C: Placenta
options.D: Passage

explanation: The fetus represents the passenger; if its size or presentation prevents movement through an adequate pelvis, it constitutes a passenger-related obstruction. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T010#GNS226_U4_T010_h2)

question: The presence of a pathological retraction ring, known as Bandl's ring, is a classic warning sign of which critical condition?

options.A: Normal second stage progress
options.B: Hypertonic uterine inertia
options.C: Premature rupture of membranes
options.D: Impending uterine rupture

explanation: Bandl's ring forms when the upper uterine segment thickens and rises while the lower segment stretches thin, signaling extreme risk of uterine rupture. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T010#GNS226_U4_T010_h3)

question: A woman arrives at a rural Nigerian clinic after labouring at home for 36 hours. She exhibits tachycardia, dry lips, concentrated urine, and a high-rising contraction ring. What is the priority nursing action?

options.A: Encourage walking and stair climbing to speed up fetal descent
options.B: Administer high-dose oxytocin infusion to overcome uterine fatigue
options.C: Initiate immediate emergency medical notification and prepare for surgical intervention
options.D: Advise the patient to push forcefully during the next contraction

explanation: A patient with signs of obstructed and prolonged labour requires urgent medical escalation and surgical preparation rather than stimulation of contractions or pushing. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T010#GNS226_U4_T010_h3)

question: Vesicovaginal fistula (VVF), a devastating complication of prolonged obstructed labour, is primarily caused by which process?

options.A: Bacterial infection of the amniotic fluid
options.B: Ischemic necrosis of compressed soft tissues
options.C: Direct surgical laceration during delivery
options.D: Severe systemic maternal hypertension

explanation: Prolonged pressure from the fetal head against the pelvis cuts off blood supply to the intervening vaginal and bladder walls, leading to tissue death and fistula formation. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T010#GNS226_U4_T010_h4)

question: Why is postpartum hemorrhage a frequent consequence of prolonged labour?

options.A: The myometrium becomes exhausted and fails to contract effectively after delivery
options.B: Clotting factors are completely consumed during the early latent phase
options.C: The placenta implants abnormally deep into the myometrial wall
options.D: High oxytocin levels destroy platelets within the maternal circulation

explanation: Uterine inertia and muscular fatigue prevent the uterine muscle fibers from properly retracting around blood vessels post-delivery, resulting in atonic bleeding. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T010#GNS226_U4_T010_h4)

question: What is the primary reason for encouraging frequent bladder emptying or catheterization during prolonged labour?

options.A: Full bladders release hormones that stop uterine contractions
options.B: Urine retention prevents the kidneys from filtering medication
options.C: Bladder fullness directly causes immediate placental abruption
options.D: A full bladder displaces the uterus and can impede fetal descent

explanation: An overdistended bladder occupies pelvic space, interferes with normal uterine action, and blocks the downward movement of the presenting part. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T010#GNS226_U4_T010_h5)

question: Which maternal position should nurses discourage when managing a patient in prolonged labour?

options.A: Supine position
options.B: Lateral position
options.C: Upright kneeling
options.D: Sitting upright

explanation: The supine position causes the heavy gravid uterus to compress the vena cava and aorta, reducing maternal cardiac output and causing fetal hypoxia. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T010#GNS226_U4_T010_h5)

question: Which intervention is strictly CONTRAINDICATED when a diagnosis of cephalopelvic disproportion (CPD) has been confirmed?

options.A: Oxytocin augmentation infusion
options.B: Preparation for emergency cesarean section
options.C: Continuous fetal heart rate monitoring
options.D: Intravenous fluid hydration therapy

explanation: Stimulating contractions with oxytocin when a mechanical obstruction prevents delivery will cause uterine rupture and catastrophic harm. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T010#GNS226_U4_T010_h6)

question: What is the primary purpose of performing an amniotomy during dysfunctional labour?

options.A: To administer local anesthesia directly to the cervix
options.B: To prevent the development of maternal gestational diabetes
options.C: To release prostaglandins and improve uterine contraction efficiency
options.D: To measure internal core body temperature accurately

explanation: Rupturing membranes releases local prostaglandins and brings the presenting part into direct contact with the cervix, strengthening labour progress. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T010#GNS226_U4_T010_h6)

question: What is the primary clinical function of the WHO partograph during labour management?

options.A: To provide early visual warning of abnormal labour progress
options.B: To calculate exact birth weight prior to delivery
options.C: To determine the precise blood type of the neonate
options.D: To serve as a permanent legal financial billing record

explanation: The partograph tracks cervical dilation and maternal-fetal well-being graphically, allowing clinicians to spot deviations from normal progress early. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T010#GNS226_U4_T010_h7)

question: Which strategy is most effective at the community level in reducing the incidence of severe prolonged labour in Nigeria?

options.A: Encouraging prolonged bed rest throughout the third trimester
options.B: Relying exclusively on herbal oxytocics administered at home
options.C: Restricting oral fluid intake during all stages of pregnancy
options.D: Promoting skilled birth attendance and early hospital referral

explanation: Educating communities to seek care from skilled birth attendants ensures timely detection of abnormalities and prevents delayed referrals. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T010#GNS226_U4_T010_h7)

question: What is the primary difference between an episiotomy and an obstetric laceration?

options.A: An episiotomy requires suturing but lacerations always heal without intervention.
options.B: Lacerations only occur in the vaginal mucosa whereas episiotomies involve muscle.
options.C: Lacerations are performed by obstetricians while episiotomies are done by midwives.
options.D: An episiotomy is a controlled surgical incision while a laceration is an accidental tear.

explanation: Surgical incisions have clean, predictable margins made with scissors or a blade, whereas tears feature ragged edges caused by mechanical stretching beyond tissue limits. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T011#GNS226_U4_T011_h1)

question: Why is prompt anatomical repair of deep perineal and genital tears necessary?

options.A: To restore normal function and prevent long-term morbidity
options.B: To ensure immediate cessation of lochia rubra flow
options.C: To accelerate the process of normal postpartum uterine involution
options.D: To prevent the development of postpartum pre-eclampsia

explanation: Accurate realignment of torn muscular and fascial planes ensures proper healing, preserves urinary and fecal continence, and avoids chronic pain. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T011#GNS226_U4_T011_h1)

question: What is the primary structural role of the perineal body during childbirth?

options.A: It controls the hormonal triggers that initiate the second stage of labour.
options.B: It forms the rigid bony framework of the lower pelvic outlet.
options.C: It secretes lubricating fluids to ease the passage of the fetal head.
options.D: It acts as a central tendon and anchor point for multiple perineal muscles.

explanation: The perineal body provides structural integrity to the pelvic floor by uniting several muscles of the perineum in a dense fibromuscular node. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T011#GNS226_U4_T011_h2)

question: Which muscle group forms the primary supportive sling of the pelvic floor?

options.A: Abdominal rectus muscles
options.B: Internal obturator muscles
options.C: Gluteus maximus muscles
options.D: Levator ani muscle group

explanation: The levator ani muscles wrap around the vagina, urethra, and rectum to maintain pelvic organ support and maintain continence. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T011#GNS226_U4_T011_h2)

question: A perineal tear that involves the vaginal mucosa and perineal muscles but leaves the anal sphincter intact is classified as what degree?

options.A: Fourth-degree tear
options.B: Second-degree tear
options.C: Third-degree tear
options.D: First-degree tear

explanation: Second-degree tears involve the perineal muscles and skin/mucosa but do not extend into the anal sphincter complex. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T011#GNS226_U4_T011_h3)

question: Which classification of perineal trauma involves disruption of the rectal mucosa?

options.A: Fourth-degree tear
options.B: Second-degree tear
options.C: Third-degree tear
options.D: First-degree tear

explanation: A fourth-degree tear is the most extensive classification, characterized by injury to the anal sphincters as well as the epithelium of the rectum. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T011#GNS226_U4_T011_h3)

question: Which patient group is statistically at the highest risk for severe perineal lacerations?

options.A: Nulliparous women experiencing a rapid instrumental delivery
options.B: Multiparous women with a history of precipitous deliveries
options.C: Multiparous women delivering a low birth weight infant
options.D: Women undergoing an elective Caesarean section at term

explanation: First-time mothers have tighter, unstretched perineal tissues, and instruments further increase the risk of soft tissue trauma. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T011#GNS226_U4_T011_h4)

question: What is the primary mechanism by which a persistent occipitoposterior position causes perineal tearing?

options.A: It causes premature rupture of membranes and uterine hyperstimulation.
options.B: It directly damages the anal sphincter prior to the onset of crowning.
options.C: It presents a wider fetal head diameter to the pelvic outlet, increasing stretching.
options.D: It prevents the engagement of the fetal head in the pelvic brim.

explanation: An occipitoposterior position forces the fetal head to deflex, presenting a larger circumference that strains the perineal tissues. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T011#GNS226_U4_T011_h4)

question: When should the initial comprehensive inspection of the perineum and vagina take place?

options.A: Twenty-four hours after the completion of the third stage
options.B: Prior to the onset of the second stage of labour
options.C: Immediately after the rupture of fetal membranes
options.D: Immediately following the delivery of the placenta

explanation: Postpartum assessment of the genital tract is routinely performed immediately after placental delivery to identify and repair trauma promptly. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T011#GNS226_U4_T011_h5)

question: A midwife suspects a third-degree perineal tear after a difficult vacuum delivery. What specific assessment step is mandatory to confirm this?

options.A: Administer a local anesthetic block before touching the area
options.B: Catheterize the bladder to check for hematuria and urethral tears
options.C: Measure the depth of the vaginal wall laceration with a sterile ruler
options.D: Perform a digital rectal examination to check anal sphincter tone

explanation: A rectal examination allows the clinician to palpate the sphincter muscles and assess if the internal or external sphincters are disrupted. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T011#GNS226_U4_T011_h5)

question: Which type of suture material is standard for repairing perineal lacerations?

options.A: Synthetic absorbable sutures
options.B: Metallic stainless steel wire
options.C: Non-absorbable silk sutures
options.D: Untreated natural catgut

explanation: Synthetic absorbable materials provide adequate tensile strength during initial healing and break down naturally without requiring removal. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T011#GNS226_U4_T011_h6)

question: When repairing a vaginal and perineal laceration, where should suturing typically begin?

options.A: At the lateral labial margins
options.B: At the apex of the vaginal tear
options.C: At the external anal sphincter
options.D: At the midpoint of the perineal skin

explanation: Starting at the apex of the vaginal component allows the clinician to locate the highest point of the wound and secure hemostasis before closing inferiorly. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T011#GNS226_U4_T011_h6)

question: What is the primary purpose of applying a cold pack to the perineum in the first twenty-four hours post-repair?

options.A: To stimulate rapid closure of the vaginal apex
options.B: To encourage early postpartum micturition
options.C: To prevent the development of lochia rubra
options.D: To minimize local edema and reduce pain

explanation: Cold therapy induces vasoconstriction, which decreases swelling and numbs nerve endings to provide immediate pain relief. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T011#GNS226_U4_T011_h7)

question: Why is dietary management involving high-fiber foods emphasized following a deep perineal repair?

options.A: To prevent constipation and avoid straining on the sutures
options.B: To stimulate increased production of breast milk for the infant
options.C: To accelerate the natural absorption of synthetic suture material
options.D: To prevent postpartum anemia by improving iron absorption

explanation: Soft stools reduce the physical pressure and mechanical strain placed on the newly repaired perineal muscles and anal sphincter complex during defecation. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T011#GNS226_U4_T011_h7)

question: Which of the following is NOT a recognized short-term complication of poor perineal repair? (Select the negative frame)

options.A: Pelvic organ prolapse caused by decade-long muscle atrophy
options.B: Wound dehiscence and localized infection of the sutures
options.C: Local wound hematoma formation within the soft tissues
options.D: Excessive postpartum hemorrhage from bleeding vessels

explanation: Pelvic organ prolapse is a long-term consequence of support failure, whereas hemorrhage, hematoma, and dehiscence occur immediately in the postpartum period. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T011#GNS226_U4_T011_h8)

question: What is a common long-term consequence for women with an unrecognized third- or fourth-degree perineal tear?

options.A: Chronic postpartum hypertension
options.B: Permanent cessation of menstruation
options.C: Fecal or flatal incontinence
options.D: Recurrent gestational diabetes

explanation: Disruption of the anal sphincter complex that goes unrepaired permanently impairs bowel control, leading to involuntary loss of gas or stool. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T011#GNS226_U4_T011_h8)

question: What is the traditional definition of primary postpartum haemorrhage following a vaginal delivery?

options.A: Bleeding occurring strictly after the first week of delivery
options.B: Blood loss exceeding 1000 mL within 24 hours of birth
options.C: Blood loss exceeding 500 mL within 24 hours of birth
options.D: Any bleeding requiring a blood transfusion post-delivery

explanation: Primary postpartum haemorrhage is defined as a blood loss of 500 mL or more from the genital tract within the first 24 hours following a vaginal delivery. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T012#GNS226_U4_T012_h1)

question: How is secondary postpartum haemorrhage clinically distinguished from primary postpartum haemorrhage?

options.A: It is exclusively caused by severe postpartum hypertension
options.B: It only happens following a surgical caesarean section
options.C: It involves a fixed blood loss volume of exactly 500 mL
options.D: It occurs between 24 hours and 12 weeks after delivery

explanation: While primary PPH happens within the first 24 hours, secondary PPH manifests from 24 hours up to 12 weeks postpartum, often due to retained products of conception. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T012#GNS226_U4_T012_h1)

question: What is the most common cause of primary postpartum haemorrhage among the 4 Ts?

options.A: Trauma
options.B: Tissue
options.C: Thrombin
options.D: Tone

explanation: Uterine atony, represented by 'Tone', is responsible for the vast majority of primary postpartum haemorrhage cases globally. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T012#GNS226_U4_T012_h2)

question: A patient with a firmly contracted uterus continues to experience steady bright red bleeding following a vaginal delivery. Which category of the 4 Ts is most likely implicated?

options.A: Trauma
options.B: Toxemia
options.C: Tone
options.D: Thrombin

explanation: When bleeding persists despite a hard, well-contracted uterus, the cause is typically anatomical trauma such as a cervical or vaginal laceration. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T012#GNS226_U4_T012_h2)

question: Which condition is a classic example of uterine overdistension that increases the risk of postpartum haemorrhage?

options.A: Multiple gestation
options.B: Primary maternal hypertension
options.C: Iron deficiency anemia
options.D: Gestational diabetes

explanation: Carrying twins or higher-order multiples overstretches the myometrial fibers, predisposing the uterus to atony following delivery. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T012#GNS226_U4_T012_h3)

question: Why is grand multiparity considered a major risk factor for postpartum haemorrhage?

options.A: It causes an immediate drop in maternal platelet counts
options.B: It completely prevents the placenta from forming normally
options.C: It leads to decreased elasticity and fatigue of the myometrium
options.D: It induces chronic hypotension throughout pregnancy

explanation: Repeated pregnancies stretch and weaken the uterine muscle fibers over time, reducing their ability to contract effectively after birth. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T012#GNS226_U4_T012_h3)

question: What is the recommended first-line uterotonic medication for the active management of the third stage of labour?

options.A: Magnesium sulfate
options.B: Oxytocin
options.C: Misoprostol
options.D: Ergometrine

explanation: Oxytocin is universally recommended as the primary uterotonic due to its rapid onset, high efficacy, and minimal side effect profile. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T012#GNS226_U4_T012_h4)

question: What is the primary physiological purpose of applying controlled cord traction during the third stage of labour?

options.A: To force retained lochia out of the uterine cavity
options.B: To facilitate the prompt and safe delivery of the placenta
options.C: To stimulate maternal cortisol production and milk letdown
options.D: To stretch the lower uterine segment and prevent atony

explanation: Controlled cord traction helps deliver the placenta efficiently while minimizing the risk of cord snapping or uterine inversion. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T012#GNS226_U4_T012_h4)

question: What is typically the earliest physiological sign of significant blood loss in a postpartum patient?

options.A: Unconsciousness
options.B: A drop in body temperature
options.C: Tachycardia
options.D: Severe hypotension

explanation: Tachycardia appears early because the body compensates for reduced blood volume by increasing the heart rate to maintain cardiac output. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T012#GNS226_U4_T012_h5)

question: How is the shock index calculated during the assessment of a postpartum hemorrhage patient?

options.A: Systolic blood pressure divided by heart rate
options.B: Heart rate divided by systolic blood pressure
options.C: Respiratory rate multiplied by diastolic pressure
options.D: Total blood loss volume divided by body weight

explanation: The shock index is computed by dividing the patient's heart rate by their systolic blood pressure, providing a sensitive indicator of hemodynamic stability. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T012#GNS226_U4_T012_h5)

question: Which adjunct medication is recommended to be administered intravenously early in a postpartum haemorrhage protocol to reduce clot breakdown?

options.A: Calcium gluconate
options.B: Sodium bicarbonate
options.C: Vitamin K injection
options.D: Tranexamic acid

explanation: Tranexamic acid is an antifibrinolytic agent proven to significantly reduce deaths due to postpartum bleeding when given promptly. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T012#GNS226_U4_T012_h6)

question: A postpartum patient is bleeding heavily from uterine atony, and first-line oxytocin infusions have failed to stop the hemorrhage. What is the most appropriate immediate physical maneuver to attempt next?

options.A: Application of a cold pelvic ice pack
options.B: Bimanual compression of the uterus
options.C: Immediate emergency subtotal hysterectomy
options.D: Strict bed rest and observation for one hour

explanation: Bimanual compression is a rapid, non-surgical bedside intervention that mechanically compresses open blood vessels while awaiting surgical preparations. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T012#GNS226_U4_T012_h6)

question: What size of intravenous cannula is ideally established for aggressive fluid and blood resuscitation in severe postpartum haemorrhage?

options.A: 22-gauge or 24-gauge
options.B: 20-gauge or 22-gauge
options.C: 16-gauge or 18-gauge
options.D: 14-gauge pediatric size

explanation: Large-bore cannulae (16G or 18G) are required to allow rapid infusion of viscous blood products and large volumes of crystalloids under pressure. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T012#GNS226_U4_T012_h7)

question: Why is the insertion of an indwelling urinary catheter with a urometer essential during the management of severe postpartum haemorrhage?

options.A: To monitor renal perfusion and prevent acute kidney injury
options.B: To prevent the bladder from becoming distended and displacing the uterus
options.C: To collect clean-catch urine specimens for routine urinalysis
options.D: To measure specific gravity and confirm maternal hydration status

explanation: A full urinary catheter with a urometer allows precise, hourly tracking of urine output, serving as a key indicator of adequate kidney perfusion during shock. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T012#GNS226_U4_T012_h7)

question: What is the term for ischemic necrosis of the anterior pituitary gland resulting from severe postpartum hemorrhage and hypotension?

options.A: Sheehan syndrome
options.B: Asherman syndrome
options.C: HELLP syndrome
options.D: Cushing syndrome

explanation: Sheehan syndrome occurs when severe blood loss leads to pituitary ischemia, resulting in panhypopituitarism often presenting with lactation failure. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T012#GNS226_U4_T012_h8)

question: Which of the following is NOT a direct physical complication of severe acute postpartum haemorrhage?

options.A: Dilutional coagulopathy
options.B: Acute kidney injury
options.C: Hemorrhagic shock
options.D: Gestational diabetes mellitus

explanation: Gestational diabetes is a metabolic condition related to insulin resistance during pregnancy, whereas acute kidney injury, coagulopathy, and shock are direct complications of major blood loss. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T012#GNS226_U4_T012_h8)

question: What is a primary clinical consequence of unsafe abortion frequently seen in Nigerian emergency wards?

options.A: Severe hemorrhage and sepsis
options.B: Pathological fetal malpresentation
options.C: Chronic gestational hypertension
options.D: Gestational diabetes mellitus

explanation: Unsafe abortion procedures frequently lead to acute blood loss and severe pelvic infections due to unsterile techniques. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T001#GNS226_U5_T001_h1)

question: Why do many women experience delayed treatment following complications from an unsafe procedure?

question: A patient scheduled for MVA expresses severe anxiety and fear of pain. What initial nursing action is most appropriate?

options.A: Administer immediate intravenous sedatives without further discussion
options.B: Reschedule the procedure for a later date under general anesthesia
options.C: Provide empathetic listening, explain the steps, and discuss pain relief options
options.D: Advise her that discomfort is minimal and requires no intervention

question: What instrument is used to grasp the anterior lip of the cervix and straighten the uterocervical axis?

options.B: Single-tooth tenaculum
options.C: Sponge-holding forceps
options.D: Bivalve speculum

question: How does the clinician ensure complete evacuation of the uterine contents once the cannula is inside the cavity?

options.A: By clamping the cervical os tightly with sponge forceps

question: What is the primary reason for inspecting the evacuated tissue in a strainer after an MVA?

question: Which nursing intervention is essential during the immediate recovery phase following an MVA?

question: What is the classic clinical sign that suggests a uterine perforation has occurred during instrumentation?

question: A patient returns to the clinic five days post-MVA with lower abdominal pain, foul-smelling vaginal discharge, and fever. What complication is most likely?

options.A: Delayed uterine perforation

question: What is the first step in processing MVA instruments immediately after a procedure is completed?

options.A: Decontamination in a 0.5% chlorine solution

question: Why is medical-grade silicone oil applied to the O-rings of an MVA syringe during reprocessing?

options.A: To prevent rust formation on metallic components

options.C: To accelerate the drying process after high-level disinfection
options.D: To maintain an airtight vacuum seal within the cylinder

question: What is the primary mechanism by which a medication abortion terminates a pregnancy?

options.A: Freezing of the gestational sac using cryotherapy

options.D: Pharmaceutical agents inducing a process similar to a miscarriage

question: Why is understanding the gestational age limit crucial for medication abortion?

options.A: Surgical backup is physically impossible once the second trimester begins
options.B: Patients develop permanent immunity to the medications after a certain week

question: What is the primary pharmacological action of mifepristone?

options.A: Prostaglandin F2-alpha stimulation
options.B: Estrogen synthesis inhibition
options.C: Oxytocin receptor blockade
options.D: Progesterone receptor antagonism

explanation: Mifepristone blocks progesterone receptors, leading to the breakdown of the decidua and cervical softening. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T011#GNS226_U5_T011_h2)

question: What role does misoprostol play when administered after mifepristone?

options.A: Stimulates uterine contractions to expel the pregnancy tissue
options.B: Neutralizes remaining hormones in the systemic circulation
options.C: Prevents nausea and vomiting caused by the first drug

question: Which condition is an absolute contraindication for a medication abortion regimen?

options.A: Mild iron-deficiency anemia

question: A client presents requesting a medication abortion, and transvaginal ultrasound reveals an intrauterine pregnancy alongside a copper IUD. What must happen first?

options.A: Antibiotics must be administered to cover potential IUD-related infections
options.B: The medical regimen can proceed immediately with the IUD left in situ

question: Why is Rh blood typing clinically necessary before administering a medication abortion?

question: What is an essential component of pre-procedure counseling for a medical abortion?

options.A: Requiring mandatory psychiatric clearance before any medications are dispensed
options.B: Instructing the client to avoid all oral hydration during the process
options.C: Guarantees that the procedure will be entirely painless from start to finish
options.D: Preparing the patient for the level of cramping and bleeding they will experience

explanation: Setting clear expectations about heavy bleeding and cramping helps reduce anxiety and prevents panic when symptoms peak. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T011#GNS226_U5_T011_h4)

question: What is the typical time interval recommended between taking mifepristone and administering misoprostol?

options.A: Immediately back-to-back

options.D: Exactly one full week

question: How does incorrect sequencing or timing of the two abortion medications affect the outcome?

options.A: It turns the medical abortion into a permanent surgical sterilization

options.C: It can significantly reduce the overall efficacy of the termination process
options.D: It neutralizes all side effects but leaves the pregnancy completely unaffected

explanation: The protocol relies on the priming action of the first drug to make the uterine contractions of the second drug effective. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T011#GNS226_U5_T011_h5)

question: Which systemic symptom is commonly caused by misoprostol during a medication abortion?

options.A: Severe hypertension requiring hospitalization
options.B: Transient chills and low-grade fever
options.C: Paralysis of the lower extremities
options.D: Permanent loss of deep tendon reflexes

question: How should a nurse interpret reports of heavy bleeding and strong cramping shortly after taking misoprostol?

options.A: As expected signs that the treatment is successfully inducing tissue expulsion
options.B: As proof that the mifepristone dose failed to absorb properly
options.C: As a sign of severe allergic hypersensitivity to the prostaglandin

question: What clinical threshold defines excessive post-abortion hemorrhage requiring urgent evaluation?

question: Which combination of symptoms is most characteristic of post-abortion infection?

question: When can a patient typically start a new method of contraception following a medication abortion?

options.A: Only after surgical confirmation of complete endometrial healing

options.C: Immediately on the day of treatment or at the follow-up visit

question: Why is timely post-abortion follow-up essential for clinical quality care?

explanation: A follow-up check verifies that the medical abortion was fully successful and catches any incomplete evacuations early. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T011#GNS226_U5_T011_h8)

question: What is the primary pharmacological purpose of combining mifepristone and misoprostol in medication abortion?

options.A: To prevent postpartum hemorrhage through sustained vasoconstriction

options.D: To sequentially disrupt pregnancy maintenance and induce uterine evacuation

question: Why is the sequential order of administering mifepristone followed by misoprostol clinically necessary?

options.A: Reversing the sequence causes immediate severe systemic toxicity and allergic shock
options.B: Mifepristone primes the myometrium and decidua, making subsequent contractions by misoprostol effective

options.D: Misoprostol must soften the cervix before mifepristone can enter the bloodstream safely

question: Which cellular receptor does mifepristone primarily block to initiate medication abortion?

options.A: Estrogen receptor
options.B: Prostaglandin receptor
options.C: Progesterone receptor

question: What is the direct pharmacological action of misoprostol on the uterus?

options.B: It blocks nerve conduction in the pelvis to eliminate procedural pain

question: Which condition must be definitively ruled out before administering a medication abortion regimen?

question: A patient requesting medication abortion is found to have an intrauterine device currently in place. What is the appropriate clinical action?

question: What is the standard oral dose of mifepristone typically administered in early medication abortion protocols?

question: What is a primary advantage of administering misoprostol via the vaginal route compared to the oral route?

question: Which medication class is typically recommended for managing cramping pain during a medication abortion?

question: Which symptom experienced shortly after taking misoprostol is considered a normal, self-limiting pharmacological side effect rather than a sign of infection?

question: A patient returns to the clinic reporting severe pelvic pain and a temperature of 38.8°C three days after taking misoprostol, along with purulent vaginal discharge. What is the most likely underlying condition?

question: When is it clinically appropriate to initiate short-acting hormonal contraceptives or implants after a medication abortion?

question: According to the Nigerian Criminal Code, what is the primary legal justification for performing an abortion?

question: What is the professional and ethical obligation of a Nigerian nurse when treating a patient presenting with complications from an incomplete abortion?

options.B: Delay treatment until family members arrive to grant formal consent

question: What is the primary pharmacological class of misoprostol?

question: Why is the misoprostol-only regimen particularly valuable in resource-constrained healthcare settings?

options.B: It prevents all post-abortion infections without antibiotics

question: How does misoprostol affect the cervix prior to fetal expulsion?

question: Which administration route achieves peak plasma concentrations the fastest?

question: What condition MUST be ruled out before administering a misoprostol-only regimen?

question: A client presents to the clinic with confirmed incomplete abortion and retained products of conception. What is the primary role of misoprostol in this scenario?

question: Which instruction is critical when administering misoprostol via the buccal route?

question: Which of the following is an absolute contraindication for a misoprostol-only regimen?

question: What key information should be included in pre-procedure counseling regarding bleeding expectations?

question: What bleeding threshold is widely used to define excessive hemorrhage requiring urgent medical evaluation?

question: When does a client's ovulatory cycle and fertility typically return following a medical abortion?

question: When is the most appropriate time to initiate a new contraceptive method for a client undergoing a misoprostol-only regimen?

question: What is widely recognized in clinical practice as the fifth vital sign?

question: Why is proactive pain assessment particularly vital in post-abortion care?

question: What is the primary physiological cause of cramping pain following uterine evacuation?

options.A: Myometrial smooth muscle contractions
options.B: Rapid fluctuation in systemic estrogen
options.C: Vaginal mucosal stretching
options.D: Inflammation of the peritoneal lining

explanation: The uterus contracts forcefully after emptying to compress open blood vessels and achieve hemostasis, which generates typical cramping pain. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T014#GNS226_U5_T014_h2)

question: How does mechanical cervical dilation contribute to post-procedure discomfort?

options.A: By inducing immediate systemic hypotension
options.B: By blocking local pelvic nerve conduction
options.C: By preventing normal myometrial involution
options.D: By stimulating local nociceptors through physical stretching

explanation: Forcing the internal and external cervical os to open stretches nerve endings in the cervix, resulting in acute somatic pain signals sent to the spinal cord. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T014#GNS226_U5_T014_h2)

question: What does a numeric pain rating scale typically range between in standard clinical assessment?

options.A: Zero to one hundred
options.B: Zero to ten
options.C: One to five
options.D: Minus five to plus five

explanation: The standard numeric rating scale uses zero to represent no pain and ten to represent the worst imaginable pain. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T014#GNS226_U5_T014_h3)

question: A patient reports a pain score of 8 out of 10 shortly after a surgical termination. What is the most appropriate initial nursing action?

options.A: Perform a comprehensive evaluation of pain characteristics and notify the prescriber for stronger analgesia
options.B: Reassure the patient that high pain scores are normal and require no medication
options.C: Restrict fluid intake to prevent further uterine cramping
options.D: Discharge the patient immediately to recover in a familiar home environment

explanation: A high pain score indicates inadequate relief, necessitating a thorough assessment and prompt escalation of analgesic therapy. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T014#GNS226_U5_T014_h3)

question: What is the primary mechanism by which NSAIDs reduce post-abortion cramping?

options.A: Decreasing systemic blood pressure
options.B: Inhibiting prostaglandin synthesis
options.C: Inducing skeletal muscle relaxation
options.D: Blocking central opioid receptors

explanation: NSAIDs target cyclooxygenase enzymes to decrease prostaglandin production, directly reducing the intensity of uterine contractions and associated pain. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T014#GNS226_U5_T014_h4)

question: Why is multi-modal analgesia often recommended for managing procedural and post-procedural pain?

options.A: It ensures patients remain heavily sedated throughout their hospital stay
options.B: It eliminates the need for any nursing assessment of pain scores
options.C: Combining medications with different mechanisms provides superior relief while minimizing individual drug side effects
options.D: Single-drug therapy is illegal in most healthcare jurisdictions

explanation: Using different classes of drugs targets various pain pathways simultaneously, allowing lower doses of each agent and reducing adverse reactions. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T014#GNS226_U5_T014_h4)

question: Which non-pharmacological intervention helps relax lower abdominal muscle tension and ease cramping?

options.A: Applying a warm compress to the abdomen
options.B: Encouraging high-intensity physical pacing
options.C: Placing an ice pack directly on the lower back
options.D: Administering cold intravenous fluids

explanation: Warmth promotes local vasodilation and relaxes smooth muscle tissue in the myometrium, helping to alleviate cramping discomfort. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T014#GNS226_U5_T014_h5)

question: A recovering patient expresses severe anxiety alongside mild uterine cramping. Which nursing action best addresses both symptoms simultaneously?

options.A: Guiding the patient through slow, deep breathing exercises while offering a reassuring presence
options.B: Leaving the patient alone in a dark room until sedation wears off completely
options.C: Administering a high dose of intravenous antibiotics
options.D: Insisting that anxiety is unrelated to physical recovery

explanation: Deep breathing and supportive communication calm the autonomic nervous system, reducing both anxiety and the perception of pain. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T014#GNS226_U5_T014_h5)

question: Which clinical finding represents a major red flag indicating potential post-abortion complications?

options.A: Low-grade fatigue following a general anesthetic
options.B: Light spotting that gradually decreases over one week
options.C: Mild intermittent cramping during the first forty-eight hours
options.D: Severe lower abdominal pain unresponsive to standard oral analgesics

explanation: Pain that worsens or fails to respond to appropriate medication suggests surgical complications like infection, retained tissue, or perforation. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T014#GNS226_U5_T014_h6)

question: What is the primary danger of failing to recognize abnormal pain patterns associated with retained products of conception?

options.A: Immediate onset of chronic hypertension
options.B: Permanent loss of bladder control within hours
options.C: Development of irreversible skin rashes
options.D: Development of severe hemorrhage and pelvic infection

explanation: Retained tissue prevents the uterus from contracting fully, increasing the risk of heavy bleeding and bacterial proliferation leading to sepsis. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T014#GNS226_U5_T014_h6)

question: What is an essential component of discharge education for a patient recovering from an abortion procedure?

options.A: Immediate cessation of all prescribed pain medications
options.B: A strict requirement to remain on bed rest for two full weeks
options.C: Verbal instructions only, without any written documentation
options.D: Clear instructions on medication schedules and warning signs of complications

explanation: Written and verbal guidance regarding medication use and red-flag symptoms ensures safe self-management at home. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T014#GNS226_U5_T014_h7)

question: Why is providing written discharge information crucial alongside verbal explanations?

options.A: Hospital accreditation standards forbid verbal-only discharges
options.B: Written instructions replace the need for any follow-up clinical appointments
options.C: Patients may experience residual effects from medications or stress that impair memory retention
options.D: It guarantees that patients will never experience any side effects

explanation: Post-procedure fatigue, stress, and medication side effects make it difficult to remember complex verbal instructions without written reinforcement. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T014#GNS226_U5_T014_h7)

question: What is the earliest recorded time frame for the return of ovulation following an abortion?

options.A: Two to three months
options.B: Immediately upon menses
options.C: Four to six weeks
options.D: Eight to ten days

explanation: Ovulation can resume as early as eight to ten days after pregnancy termination, meaning unprotected intercourse during this early window can result in rapid repeat conception. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T015#GNS226_U5_T015_h1)

question: Why is immediate post-abortion contraceptive counseling prioritized in clinical practice?

options.A: Patients are incapable of making decisions regarding family planning later
options.B: Hormonal methods interfere with uterine involution if delayed
options.C: Hospital policy mandates permanent sterilization after pregnancy loss
options.D: Fertility returns rapidly before the first normal menstrual cycle begins

explanation: Because ovulation precedes menses, waiting for a normal menstrual period before starting contraception exposes the patient to the risk of an unplanned pregnancy. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T015#GNS226_U5_T015_h1)

question: A client-centered approach to post-abortion family planning is best defined as which of the following?

options.A: Prioritizing hospital discharge speed over detailed method explanation
options.B: Strongly recommending long-acting methods to every single patient
options.C: Leaving the choice entirely to chance without clinical guidance
options.D: Facilitating informed choices aligned with the client's personal life goals

explanation: Client-centered care prioritizes the individual's unique preferences, values, and life circumstances rather than imposing a provider-driven agenda. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T015#GNS226_U5_T015_h2)

question: Which assessment step is crucial before recommending a combined hormonal contraceptive to a post-abortion client?

options.A: Evaluating religious affiliation regarding family size
options.B: Measuring baseline pelvic floor muscle strength
options.C: Screening for cardiovascular risk factors and blood pressure
options.D: Confirming complete cessation of all uterine cramping

explanation: Combined hormonal contraceptives contain estrogen, which increases the risk of thromboembolism, making cardiovascular screening mandatory. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T015#GNS226_U5_T015_h2)

question: What is the primary advantage of immediate post-abortion contraceptive initiation?

options.A: It eliminates the need for a separate return clinic visit
options.B: It completely stops all post-procedural uterine bleeding
options.C: It guarantees lifelong protection against unintended pregnancy
options.D: It removes all potential side effects associated with hormones

explanation: Providing contraception before the patient leaves reduces loss to follow-up and ensures immediate protection against subsequent unplanned pregnancies. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T015#GNS226_U5_T015_h3)

question: A patient presents with signs of an acute pelvic infection following an incomplete abortion. Which contraceptive management plan is most appropriate?

options.A: Prescribe high-dose oral estrogen pills to induce chemical sterilization
options.B: Insert a copper intrauterine device immediately to prevent further infection
options.C: Treat the infection and defer intrauterine device insertion until resolution
options.D: Refuse all contraceptive counseling until the patient is fully discharged

explanation: Placing an intrauterine device in the presence of an active pelvic infection risks worsening the condition and ascending pelvic inflammatory disease. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T015#GNS226_U5_T015_h3)

question: Which of the following is classified as a long-acting reversible contraceptive method?

options.A: Male latex condom
options.B: Subdermal progestin implant
options.C: Combined oral contraceptive pill
options.D: Depo-Provera injection

explanation: Subdermal implants and intrauterine devices are classified as LARC methods because they provide continuous, highly effective protection for years without requiring daily action. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T015#GNS226_U5_T015_h4)

question: What factor contributes to a slightly higher rate of intrauterine device expulsion when inserted immediately after a second-trimester abortion?

options.A: Rapid degradation of copper wiring in tissue
options.B: Increased systemic blood pressure in the client
options.C: An enlarged and relaxed uterine cavity
options.D: Severe hormone imbalances unique to second trimester

explanation: After a second-trimester abortion, the uterus is larger and its walls are less toned, making it easier for an intrauterine device to be accidentally pushed out or expelled. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T015#GNS226_U5_T015_h4)

question: What is a major clinical advantage of barrier methods compared to hormonal contraceptives?

options.A: Continuous multi-year duration of action
options.B: Higher overall effectiveness in preventing pregnancy
options.C: Complete elimination of user error
options.D: Protection against sexually transmitted infections

explanation: Barrier methods such as condoms are unique in providing dual protection by simultaneously preventing both unintended pregnancy and sexually transmitted infections. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T015#GNS226_U5_T015_h5)

question: When can progestin-only injectable contraceptives be safely administered following an abortion?

options.A: Only if the client is over the age of thirty-five
options.B: Only after three normal menstrual cycles
options.C: Exclusively after surgical evacuation, never medical
options.D: Immediately on the day of the procedure

explanation: Progestin-only injectables have no estrogen-related cardiovascular contraindications and can be administered safely on the same day as abortion care. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T015#GNS226_U5_T015_h5)

question: Which of the following is a frequent community myth regarding modern contraceptive use?

options.A: Hormonal pills cure chronic infectious diseases
options.B: Contraceptives cause permanent future infertility
options.C: Barrier methods permanently alter menstrual flow
options.D: Intrauterine devices increase bone mineral density

explanation: A pervasive misconception is that using modern contraception leads to permanent sterility, a fear that nurses must proactively address during counseling. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T015#GNS226_U5_T015_h6)

question: How should a nurse respond when a client expresses fear of weight gain from injectable contraceptives?

options.A: Force the client to accept an intrauterine device instead
options.B: Acknowledge the possibility, discuss lifestyle measures, and validate concerns
options.C: Dismiss the concern as unscientific nonsense and refuse further discussion
options.D: Guarantee that weight gain never happens to any user of the method

explanation: Validating client concerns and providing realistic information builds trust and helps clients manage potential side effects without abandoning contraception. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T015#GNS226_U5_T015_h6)

question: What is an essential component of holistic post-abortion nursing documentation?

options.A: Documenting the exact financial cost of hospital supplies used
options.B: Recording the specific contraceptive method and patient education provided
options.C: Listing the names of all family members aware of the procedure
options.D: Detailing the precise political views of the client regarding abortion

explanation: Accurate clinical records must reflect the chosen contraceptive plan, details of counseling, and follow-up instructions to ensure continuity of care. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T015#GNS226_U5_T015_h7)

question: Why is psychological support considered a vital aspect of holistic post-abortion care?

options.A: Emotional distress directly inactivates hormonal contraceptive efficacy
options.B: Psychological counseling is legally required before any prescription can be written
options.C: Mental health evaluation replaces the need for physical pelvic examinations
options.D: Clients may experience a range of complex emotional responses following termination

explanation: Abortion experiences involve varied emotional landscapes; addressing psychological well-being ensures comprehensive, patient-centered healing. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T015#GNS226_U5_T015_h7)

question: What is the primary clinical goal of integrating family planning into post-abortion care?

options.A: Preventing rapid repeat unintended pregnancies
options.B: Accelerating physical involution of the uterus
options.C: Treating underlying pelvic inflammatory disease
options.D: Permanently eliminating future fertility potential

explanation: Integrating contraception immediately after pregnancy loss provides essential protection against unintended conceptions before fertility fully resumes. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T016#GNS226_U5_T016_h1)

question: Why is the immediate post-abortion period considered a strategic window for contraceptive counselling?

options.A: Client motivation to avoid another immediate pregnancy is often very high
options.B: Hormonal contraceptives are only effective if started during this specific phase
options.C: Patients are usually detained in the hospital for observation for several weeks
options.D: Surgical complications prevent discharge until a method is chosen

explanation: The emotional and physical experience of pregnancy termination often creates a strong readiness to adopt effective contraceptive methods. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T016#GNS226_U5_T016_h1)

question: How early can ovulation return following a first-trimester abortion?

options.A: As early as two weeks post-procedure
options.B: Only after three normal menstrual cycles
options.C: Precisely six weeks to the day
options.D: After complete hormonal normalization at six months

explanation: Follicular activity restarts quickly after pregnancy termination, meaning ovulation can happen before a woman experiences her first period. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T016#GNS226_U5_T016_h2)

question: A patient asks if she needs to wait for her next menstrual period before she can safely ovulate again. What is the correct nursing response?

options.A: The uterus must shed its lining completely before a new egg can be released.
options.B: Ovulation happens before the first period, so protection is needed immediately.
options.C: Hormonal contraceptives will delay your ovulation until your period returns.
options.D: You cannot get pregnant until you have had at least two regular cycles.

explanation: Because the body releases an egg before menstruation returns, relying on the first period to signal fertility will result in unprotected exposure. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T016#GNS226_U5_T016_h2)

question: What core attitude must a nurse maintain during post-abortion contraceptive counselling?

options.A: Non-judgmental and empathetic
options.B: Skeptical and probing
options.C: Authoritative and directive
options.D: Detached and clinical

explanation: Creating a safe, stigma-free space encourages honest dialogue and ensures the client feels supported rather than judged. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T016#GNS226_U5_T016_h3)

question: Which action violates the core principle of voluntary family planning counselling?

options.A: Asking about the client's future reproductive goals in private
options.B: Insisting that a client accept a long-acting method due to parity
options.C: Explaining both the side effects and benefits of barrier methods
options.D: Providing written instructions on how to use oral contraceptive pills

explanation: Coercing or forcing a specific contraceptive choice strips the client of their fundamental right to autonomous reproductive decision-making. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T016#GNS226_U5_T016_h3)

question: Which contraceptive method protects against both pregnancy and sexually transmitted infections?

options.A: Combined oral contraceptive pills
options.B: Copper intrauterine devices
options.C: Progestin-only injectables
options.D: Condoms

explanation: Barrier methods such as condoms create a physical block that prevents the transmission of pathogens as well as sperm. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T016#GNS226_U5_T016_h4)

question: Under what primary clinical condition must the insertion of an intrauterine device be delayed following an abortion?

options.A: Presence of active pelvic infection or sepsis
options.B: Desire for future biological children within five years
options.C: History of heavy menstrual bleeding prior to pregnancy
options.D: Nulliparous status of the client

explanation: Inserting an IUD into an infected uterine cavity significantly increases the risk of ascending pelvic inflammatory disease and worsening sepsis. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T016#GNS226_U5_T016_h4)

question: When can a patient with an uncomplicated first-trimester abortion safely start a hormonal contraceptive implant?

options.A: Precisely six weeks after the medical evacuation
options.B: After completing a full course of prophylactic antibiotics
options.C: Only after waiting for a normal menstrual period
options.D: On the same day as the abortion procedure

explanation: Same-day initiation of implants and other hormonal methods is safe and ensures the client leaves protected before fertility returns. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T016#GNS226_U5_T016_h5)

question: What is the primary risk associated with inserting an intrauterine device immediately after a second-trimester abortion compared to a first-trimester procedure?

options.A: Complete failure of the device to prevent ectopic pregnancies
options.B: Higher rate of spontaneous device expulsion due to an enlarged uterine cavity
options.C: Immediate development of systemic hypertension caused by hormonal shifts
options.D: Permanent cessation of all future ovarian function

explanation: The larger surface area and dilated lower uterine segment following a second-trimester loss increase the likelihood that an IUD will be accidentally expelled. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T016#GNS226_U5_T016_h5)

question: Which of the following is NOT a common community myth regarding modern contraceptives?

options.A: They lead to severe congenital malformations
options.B: They restore normal multi-year fertility instantly
options.C: They accumulate and rot inside the abdomen
options.D: They cause permanent sterility in young women

explanation: While true that fertility returns quickly after stopping most contraceptives, the misconception is usually that they cause permanent infertility rather than instant restoration. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T016#GNS226_U5_T016_h6)

question: A client refuses an injectable contraceptive because she heard it collects in the stomach. How should the nurse respond?

options.A: Tell her that her belief is foolish and insist she takes the injection anyway.
options.B: Prescribe an oral medication instead without discussing her underlying concern.
options.C: Acknowledge her fear, then explain calmly how the medication is absorbed and metabolized by the body.
options.D: Ignore the comment and document that the client is non-compliant with care.

explanation: Addressing client concerns with respectful education builds trust and corrects misinformation without alienating the patient. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T016#GNS226_U5_T016_h6)

question: When is the standard follow-up visit typically scheduled after an uncomplicated post-abortion procedure?

options.A: Only when pregnancy occurs again
options.B: At the end of one full year
options.C: Within two weeks
options.D: After exactly six months

explanation: A two-week follow-up allows the nurse to confirm physical recovery, check for complications, and ensure the chosen contraceptive method is working well. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T016#GNS226_U5_T016_h7)

question: A client returns to the clinic three days after an abortion reporting chills, lower abdominal tenderness, and a temperature of 38.5°C. What is the most appropriate initial nursing action?

options.A: Report the findings immediately to the attending physician for evaluation of potential infection
options.B: Schedule her routine follow-up visit for two weeks later as originally planned
options.C: Discharge her with extra packs of oral contraceptive pills and tell her to rest
options.D: Reassure her that mild fever is a normal physiological reaction after uterine evacuation

explanation: Fever, chills, and abdominal pain are cardinal signs of post-abortion infection or sepsis, requiring prompt medical intervention. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T016#GNS226_U5_T016_h7)

question: What is the primary clinical goal when managing a patient with coexisting chronic illnesses undergoing post-abortion care?

options.A: Keeping underlying systemic conditions stable during the procedure
options.B: Focusing solely on the reproductive tract and ignoring baseline vitals
options.C: Discharging the patient within two hours of admission
options.D: Curing the chronic illness completely before treatment begins

explanation: The physiological stress of post-abortion care can destabilize chronic conditions, making systemic stability a primary objective. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T017#GNS226_U5_T017_h1)

question: Why is recognizing coexisting health conditions crucial in post-abortion care settings?

options.A: Untreated comorbidities can lead to acute medical decompensation during recovery
options.B: It eliminates the need for any postoperative pain management
options.C: It guarantees that the patient will never require a blood transfusion
options.D: Chronic illnesses always reverse themselves spontaneously after pregnancy

explanation: Failing to account for underlying health issues increases the risk of serious complications as the body undergoes physical stress. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T017#GNS226_U5_T017_h1)

question: What is the primary purpose of conducting medication reconciliation during an initial assessment?

options.A: Determining the exact financial cost of the patient's daily drugs
options.B: Checking for potential drug interactions with post-abortion medications
options.C: Ensuring the patient stops taking all medications permanently
options.D: Replacing all home remedies with over-the-counter vitamins

explanation: Medication reconciliation helps identify harmful clashes between home regimens and emergency or post-procedure drugs. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T017#GNS226_U5_T017_h2)

question: A patient with a known history of severe asthma is admitted for post-abortion care. Which action represents the most appropriate initial nursing priority?

options.A: Establishing baseline respiratory rate and oxygen saturation levels
options.B: Delaying assessment until the patient experiences an acute asthma attack
options.C: Administering a standard dose of a non-selective beta-blocker
options.D: Disregarding respiratory status because the procedure is gynecological

explanation: Baseline respiratory assessments allow nurses to monitor for subtle signs of respiratory compromise or drug-induced bronchospasm. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T017#GNS226_U5_T017_h2)

question: Why are patients with diabetes mellitus at a higher risk following an abortion procedure?

options.A: Insulin requirements drop to zero immediately after the procedure
options.B: Fluctuating glucose levels and altered immunity increase infection susceptibility
options.C: They are completely immune to standard antibiotic treatments
options.D: They automatically experience total renal failure within twenty-four hours

explanation: Elevated blood sugar impairs white blood cell function, making diabetic patients more vulnerable to post-abortion pelvic infections. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T017#GNS226_U5_T017_h3)

question: Which factor can trigger dangerous blood pressure spikes in a hypertensive patient recovering from an abortion?

options.A: Consuming ordinary dietary water
options.B: Complete absence of any sensory nerve endings
options.C: A sudden drop in room temperature
options.D: Acute post-procedure pain and anxiety

explanation: Pain and emotional distress activate the sympathetic nervous system, causing peripheral vasoconstriction and elevated blood pressure. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T017#GNS226_U5_T017_h3)

question: What is the immediate nursing action when managing a patient with severe post-abortion hemorrhage and profound anemia?

options.A: Administering a standard dose of an oral multivitamin tablet
options.B: Waiting for laboratory test results before taking any action
options.C: Securing large-bore intravenous access for fluid resuscitation
options.D: Instructing the patient to walk around the ward to improve circulation

explanation: Restoring intravascular volume rapidly prevents progression to irreversible hypovolemic shock. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T017#GNS226_U5_T017_h4)

question: A patient with sickle cell disease experiences a vaso-occlusive crisis following a complicated septic abortion. Which interventions form the core of immediate medical and nursing management?

options.A: Strict bed rest without any intravenous fluids or pain medication
options.B: Oxygen therapy, aggressive hydration, and appropriate pain management
options.C: Fluid restriction and immediate discharge home with oral analgesics
options.D: Immediate administration of concentrated potassium chloride boluses

explanation: Hydration and oxygenation reverse sickling and hypoxia, while pain management addresses the agonizing vaso-occlusive crisis. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T017#GNS226_U5_T017_h4)

question: Which of the following is NOT a recommended practice when providing post-abortion care to an immunocompromised patient?

options.A: Monitoring closely for signs of severe pelvic sepsis and bacteremia
options.B: Maintaining rigorous aseptic techniques during all pelvic examinations
options.C: Initiating prompt broad-spectrum antibiotics upon signs of infection
options.D: Interrupting antiretroviral therapy indefinitely to simplify the drug regimen

explanation: ART must be continued to prevent viral rebound and further immune system decline; interrupting it is unsafe. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T017#GNS226_U5_T017_h5)

question: Why are immunocompromised patients particularly vulnerable during the post-abortion recovery period?

options.A: They possess an accelerated ability to metabolize all standard antibiotics
options.B: Their blood pressure naturally drops to zero during any medical procedure
options.C: Their impaired immune response increases susceptibility to severe pelvic sepsis
options.D: They are completely immune to developing localized wound infections

explanation: Compromised immunity reduces the body's ability to fight off opportunistic pathogens introduced during uterine evacuation. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T017#GNS226_U5_T017_h5)

question: What is an effective nursing approach when caring for a post-abortion patient with a history of anxiety or depression?

options.A: Telling the patient to suppress their feelings and focus only on physical healing
options.B: Dismissing psychiatric symptoms as a normal part of every medical recovery
options.C: Avoiding all conversations regarding the patient's emotional state entirely
options.D: Providing compassionate, non-judgmental communication and emotional support

explanation: A safe, empathetic environment encourages patients to express distress without fear of stigma or judgment. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T017#GNS226_U5_T017_h6)

question: A patient exhibiting severe depressive symptoms and expressing hopelessness after an abortion should prompt which nursing action?

options.A: Withholding all pain medications to test their emotional resilience
options.B: Assuring family members that psychological distress always resolves overnight
options.C: Leaving the patient alone in a dark room until their mood improves
options.D: Arranging an immediate referral to psychiatric services or social work

explanation: Severe symptoms require professional mental health evaluation and structured multidisciplinary support. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T017#GNS226_U5_T017_h6)

question: What primary role does the nurse often play within an interprofessional post-abortion care team?

options.A: Making all final surgical decisions without consulting physicians
options.B: Acting as a central communication hub coordinating care among specialists
options.C: Prescribing specialized antiretroviral drugs independently
options.D: Handling hospital financial accounting and billing duties exclusively

explanation: Nurses coordinate treatment schedules, communicate vital signs, and bridge information gaps between different specialties. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T017#GNS226_U5_T017_h7)

question: Why are structured internal referral pathways vital for patients with complex health profiles?

options.A: They eliminate the need to monitor vital signs during the recovery period
options.B: They ensure timely specialist evaluation without dangerous administrative delays
options.C: They guarantee that the patient will never require follow-up outpatient care
options.D: They allow the nursing staff to transfer all clinical responsibility to housekeeping

explanation: Clear pathways speed up consultations with internal medicine or cardiology, protecting medically fragile patients. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T017#GNS226_U5_T017_h7)

question: Which contraceptive option is typically contraindicated for a patient with severe hypertension or a history of blood clots?

options.A: Progestin-only injectable contraceptives
options.B: The copper intrauterine device (IUD)
options.C: Barrier methods such as male and female condoms
options.D: Combined hormonal contraceptives containing estrogen and progestin

explanation: Estrogen increases the risk of thromboembolic events, making combined hormonal methods unsafe for women with clotting risks or severe vascular disease. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T017#GNS226_U5_T017_h8)

question: Why is personalized contraceptive counselling especially crucial for patients with complex medical conditions?

options.A: Personalized counselling replaces the need for any ongoing medical follow-up
options.B: Certain birth control methods can exacerbate underlying chronic illnesses
options.C: All contraceptive methods interact identically with every human organ system
options.D: Patients with chronic illnesses are legally forbidden from using implants

explanation: Selecting the right method requires matching medical eligibility criteria to prevent worsening conditions like hypertension or diabetes. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T017#GNS226_U5_T017_h8)

question: What defines an unsafe abortion procedure?

options.A: Termination performed by unskilled providers or in substandard environments
options.B: Surgical evacuation without prior general anesthesia
options.C: Termination carried out without spousal consent
options.D: Any medical termination attempted after the first trimester

explanation: The World Health Organization defines unsafe abortion by the lack of skilled providers, sterile conditions, and evidence-based standards. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T019#GNS226_U5_T019_h1)

question: Primary prevention of unsafe abortion primarily focuses on which intervention?

options.A: Prosecuting illegal abortion providers in local communities
options.B: Establishing emergency transport systems for rural clinics
options.C: Treating post-abortion hemorrhage in emergency wards
options.D: Providing universal access to modern contraception and education

explanation: Primary prevention aims to stop unintended pregnancies from happening in the first place through family planning and education. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T019#GNS226_U5_T019_h1)

question: What is the primary purpose of a healthcare referral network?

options.A: To reduce the overall financial cost of running state hospitals
options.B: To create a coordinated continuum of care across different facility levels
options.C: To eliminate the need for primary health care clinics

options.C: Obstructed labor and obstetric fistula
