explanation: The effectiveness of emergency contraceptives declines progressively the longer the patient waits to take them following unprotected intercourse. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T021#GNS226_U6_T021_h2)

question: Which of the following is a valid indication for emergency contraceptive use?

options.A: Routine daily birth control maintenance
options.B: Condom slippage or breakage during intercourse
options.C: Confirmation of a four-week established pregnancy
options.D: Treatment of pelvic inflammatory disease

explanation: Contraceptive failures, such as condom slippage or breakage, are classic indications for the use of emergency contraception. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T021#GNS226_U6_T021_h2)

question: How do hormonal emergency contraceptive pills primarily prevent pregnancy?

options.A: By destroying fertilized eggs in the fallopian tubes
options.B: By delaying or preventing ovulation
options.C: By causing immediate shedding of the uterine lining
options.D: By killing all sperm in the vaginal vault instantly

explanation: Hormonal ECPs primarily work by postponing the release of the egg from the ovary, preventing fertilization from happening in the first place. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T021#GNS226_U6_T021_h3)

question: What is true about emergency contraceptive pills once ovulation has already occurred?

options.A: They destroy the implanted embryo
options.B: They are ineffective at preventing that cycle's pregnancy
options.C: They automatically induce an immediate miscarriage
options.D: They reverse fertilization

explanation: Because ECPs work by delaying ovulation, they do not work and are ineffective if ovulation has already taken place prior to ingestion. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T021#GNS226_U6_T021_h3)

question: What is the recommended maximum time window for taking ulipristal acetate effectively?

options.A: 24 hours
options.B: 48 hours
options.C: 72 hours
options.D: 120 hours

explanation: Ulipristal acetate maintains high efficacy when taken up to 120 hours (five days) following unprotected sexual intercourse. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T021#GNS226_U6_T021_h4)

question: Which of the following is a characteristic of levonorgestrel-based emergency contraceptive pills?

options.A: They require a surgical procedure for insertion
options.B: They are typically taken as a 1.5 mg dose and work best within 72 hours
options.C: They are only effective after implantation has occurred
options.D: They always cause severe permanent sterility

explanation: Levonorgestrel is commonly taken as a single 1.5 mg dose and is most effective when utilized within the first 72 hours post-intercourse. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T021#GNS226_U6_T021_h4)

question: What makes the copper IUD unique as an emergency contraceptive method?

options.A: It must be taken orally within 24 hours
options.B: It can be left in place to provide ongoing long-term contraception
options.C: It acts exclusively by thickening cervical mucus
options.D: It is only effective if inserted before intercourse

explanation: Once inserted for emergency contraception, the copper IUD can remain in the uterus to provide years of continuous, highly effective birth control. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T021#GNS226_U6_T021_h5)

question: Within what timeframe must a copper IUD be inserted to act effectively as emergency contraception?

options.A: Within 24 hours
options.B: Within 72 hours
options.C: Within 120 hours
options.D: Within 14 days

explanation: The copper IUD is effective as an emergency contraceptive when inserted up to 120 hours (five days) after unprotected sexual intercourse. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T021#GNS226_U6_T021_h5)

question: What is a key piece of information a nurse must gather during the initial patient history for emergency contraception?

options.A: The client's favorite recreational activities
options.B: The exact time elapsed since unprotected intercourse and date of LMP
options.C: The client's complete childhood immunization record
options.D: The occupation of the client's partner

explanation: Knowing the exact time since unprotected intercourse and the date of the last menstrual period helps determine eligibility, timing windows, and existing pregnancy status. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T021#GNS226_U6_T021_h6)

question: Why is screening for previous pregnancies important before administering hormonal emergency contraception?

options.A: Because ECPs are toxic to an existing fetus
options.B: Because EC is ineffective and unnecessary if the patient is already pregnant
options.C: Because pregnancy instantly neutralizes the nurse's license
options.D: Because ECPs cause multiple gestations in pregnant women

explanation: Emergency contraception works by preventing ovulation and fertilization; if a client is already pregnant, the method serves no purpose and should not be given. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T021#GNS226_U6_T021_h6)

question: What immediate action should be considered if a patient vomits within two hours of taking an oral emergency contraceptive pill?

options.A: Immediately perform a surgical D&C
options.B: Repeat the dose because the medication may not have been absorbed
options.C: Prescribe a broad-spectrum antibiotic
options.D: Ignore the vomiting as it has no effect on efficacy

explanation: Vomiting shortly after ingestion can expel the pill, meaning the drug was likely not fully absorbed and a repeat dose may be required. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T021#GNS226_U6_T021_h7)

question: What guidance should a nurse provide regarding follow-up care after a client takes emergency contraception?

options.A: Never seek healthcare again for reproductive issues
options.B: Take a pregnancy test if menstruation is delayed by more than a week
options.C: Stop all future use of regular contraceptives permanently
options.D: Expect permanent cessation of the menstrual cycle

explanation: Clients should be instructed to take a pregnancy test if their period is delayed by more than seven days to ensure the EC was successful. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T021#GNS226_U6_T021_h7)

question: Which of the following is a common myth in Nigeria that nurses must actively dispel regarding emergency contraception?

options.A: That emergency contraception causes permanent infertility
options.B: That emergency contraception lowers blood pressure
options.C: That emergency contraception cures malaria
options.D: That emergency contraception improves vision

explanation: A widespread misconception in many communities is that emergency contraceptives cause long-term or permanent infertility, which nurses must correct with facts. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T021#GNS226_U6_T021_h8)

question: How can Nigerian nurses best support adolescents seeking reproductive health services?

options.A: By publicly shaming them to discourage future risky behavior
options.B: By providing confidential, non-judgmental, adolescent-friendly care
options.C: By refusing service unless a parent is present for every visit
options.D: By restricting access to educational pamphlets

explanation: Offering confidential, empathetic, and adolescent-friendly services helps break down barriers and encourages young people to seek proper reproductive health care. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T021#GNS226_U6_T021_h8)

question: What is the primary goal of family planning counselling in nursing practice?

options.A: To force clients to use modern contraceptives
options.B: To help clients make free, informed, and voluntary reproductive choices
options.C: To completely eliminate population growth in Nigeria
options.D: To replace medical diagnosis with reproductive advice

explanation: Family planning counselling aims to empower individuals and couples to make free, informed, and voluntary choices about their reproductive lives. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T022#GNS226_U6_T022_h1)

question: Which of the following describes the role of a nurse during family planning counselling?

options.A: A front-line provider bridging contraceptive technology and community acceptance
options.B: A strict enforcer of government family size limits
options.C: A passive observer of client decisions
options.D: A researcher focused solely on demographic statistics

explanation: Nurses act as front-line providers who connect clients with contraceptive technologies while promoting acceptance and health education. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T022#GNS226_U6_T022_h1)

question: Which ethical principle gives clients the right to make independent contraceptive choices without coercion?

options.A: Beneficence
options.B: Autonomy
options.C: Justice
options.D: Veracity

explanation: Autonomy ensures that clients have the freedom to make their own informed decisions regarding their reproductive health. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T022#GNS226_U6_T022_h2)

question: Why is confidentiality especially critical in family planning counselling within Nigerian settings?

options.A: It prevents community stigma and encourages clients to seek care freely
options.B: It allows nurses to hide medication errors from hospital management
options.C: It removes the need for documenting client medical histories
options.D: It ensures that family members can make decisions on behalf of the client

explanation: Maintaining confidentiality protects clients from societal stigma and builds the trust necessary for them to utilize services openly. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T022#GNS226_U6_T022_h2)

question: What does the letter 'T' stand for in the GATHER counselling framework?

options.A: Test the client for sexually transmitted infections
options.B: Tell the client about various contraceptive methods
options.C: Transfer the client to a medical doctor
options.D: Treat side effects immediately

explanation: In the GATHER acronym, 'T' stands for Tell, which involves providing information about available contraceptive options. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T022#GNS226_U6_T022_h3)

question: What is the primary purpose of the 'Return' step in the GATHER approach?

options.A: To collect payment for contraceptive commodities
options.B: To schedule a follow-up visit and encourage ongoing support
options.C: To return unused contraceptives to the hospital pharmacy
options.D: To review the nurse's performance with the supervisor

explanation: The 'Return' step emphasizes scheduling follow-up visits and encouraging clients to return for ongoing support or management of side effects. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T022#GNS226_U6_T022_h3)

question: Which of the following is an example of an open-ended question during family planning counselling?

options.A: Do you want to use the injectable contraceptive?
options.B: How do you feel about using family planning methods?
options.C: Did your husband send you here today?
options.D: Are you experiencing any heavy bleeding?

explanation: Asking how a client feels encourages them to elaborate and share their thoughts, unlike closed questions that require only a 'yes' or 'no'. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T022#GNS226_U6_T022_h4)

question: What is a key behavior demonstrated by a nurse practicing active listening?

options.A: Interrupting the client to correct medical misconceptions quickly
options.B: Looking away to maintain the client's privacy
options.C: Using encouraging verbal prompts and maintaining appropriate eye contact
options.D: Writing down all notes without looking at the client

explanation: Active listening involves demonstrating engagement through verbal prompts and appropriate non-verbal cues like eye contact. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T022#GNS226_U6_T022_h4)

question: Which standardized tool do nurses use to determine if a contraceptive method is medically safe for a client with underlying health conditions?

options.A: The GATHER checklist
options.B: The WHO Medical Eligibility Criteria (MEC)
options.C: The Nigerian National Health Insurance Scheme manual
options.D: The Nursing and Midwifery Council standing orders

explanation: The WHO MEC is the international standard used by healthcare providers to assess medical eligibility for various contraceptives. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T022#GNS226_U6_T022_h5)

question: Why is screening for sexually transmitted infections (STIs) important during a family planning assessment?

options.A: To prescribe antibiotics to every family planning client
options.B: To determine which hormonal pill will cure the infection
options.C: To promote dual protection strategies since most contraceptives do not protect against STIs
options.D: To prevent the client from ever using barrier methods

explanation: Most modern contraceptives do not prevent STIs, making STI screening and the promotion of dual protection crucial elements of client assessment. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T022#GNS226_U6_T022_h5)

question: What does 'informed choice' mean in the context of family planning counselling?

options.A: The nurse chooses the best method based on hospital availability
options.B: The client selects a method voluntarily after understanding all facts and options
options.C: The client's spouse makes the final decision on contraceptive use
options.D: The government dictates the most appropriate method for the community

explanation: Informed choice ensures the client makes a voluntary decision after receiving comprehensive, objective information about all available options. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T022#GNS226_U6_T022_h6)

question: How should a nurse handle a situation where a client chooses a contraceptive method that is medically unsafe for them?

options.A: Provide the method anyway to respect client autonomy
options.B: Refuse to counsel the client further
options.C: Gently explain the contraindication and guide them toward a safe alternative
options.D: Report the client to the medical director

explanation: Nurses must balance autonomy with safety by explaining medical contraindications and helping the client choose a safe, effective alternative method. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T022#GNS226_U6_T022_h6)

question: How should a nurse address a client's fear that modern contraceptives cause permanent infertility?

options.A: Confirm that long-term use permanently destroys the uterus
options.B: Dismiss the fear as unscientific and tell the client not to worry
options.C: Provide factual education explaining that fertility returns after discontinuation
options.D: Advise the client to avoid all hormonal methods permanently

explanation: Nurses must address misconceptions with facts, reassuring clients that fertility typically returns after stopping modern contraceptive methods. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T022#GNS226_U6_T022_h7)

question: Why is it important to counsel clients about potential side effects before they start a contraceptive method?

options.A: To discourage them from using any hormonal methods
options.B: To reduce anxiety, demystify normal responses, and improve method continuation
options.C: To ensure they buy extra medications from the pharmacy
options.D: To comply with hospital billing regulations

explanation: Preparing clients for expected side effects reduces panic and premature discontinuation, helping them successfully maintain their chosen method. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T022#GNS226_U6_T022_h7)

question: What is a key socio-cultural dynamic nurses must consider in Nigerian family planning counselling?

options.A: Clients always make decisions entirely independently of their families
options.B: Partners and extended family members often influence family size and contraceptive choices
options.C: Cultural beliefs have no impact on reproductive health decisions
options.D: Religious leaders strictly mandate the use of all modern contraceptives

explanation: In many Nigerian communities, family and partner influence play a significant role in reproductive decision-making, which nurses must navigate carefully. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T022#GNS226_U6_T022_h8)

question: How can nurses address financial barriers when providing family planning services in Nigeria?

options.A: By charging extra fees for private counselling sessions
options.B: By connecting clients with public health subsidized programs or community distribution networks
options.C: By advising clients to purchase expensive imported brands exclusively
options.D: By offering free inpatient admission to all contraceptive users

explanation: Connecting clients to subsidized government programs or community-based networks helps mitigate out-of-pocket financial barriers to care. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T022#GNS226_U6_T022_h8)

question: What is a primary clinical benefit of effective decision-making in family planning?

options.A: Increased population growth
options.B: Promoting optimal birth intervals
options.C: Eliminating the need for nursing assessments
options.D: Guaranteed elimination of all contraceptive side effects

explanation: Effective decision-making helps individuals determine the spacing of their children, which directly promotes optimal birth intervals and improves maternal and child health. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T023#GNS226_U6_T023_h1)

question: How should a nurse view the family planning decision-making process for a client?

options.A: As a static event that never changes
options.B: As a dynamic process that can evolve over the reproductive lifespan
options.C: As a decision that should be entirely made by the healthcare provider
options.D: As an irrelevant factor in clinical outcomes

explanation: Decision-making in family planning is dynamic and can change over time as life goals, economic status, and health conditions shift. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T023#GNS226_U6_T023_h1)

question: Which of the following best describes how cultural beliefs influence family planning in many Nigerian settings?

options.A: They completely eliminate the need for contraception
options.B: They can dictate acceptable family sizes and societal expectations of fertility
options.C: They ensure absolute gender equality in reproductive choices
options.D: They prevent any form of psychosocial anxiety

explanation: Cultural norms and beliefs frequently dictate societal expectations regarding family size and whether modern contraceptives are acceptable within that community. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T023#GNS226_U6_T023_h2)

question: Why is cultural competence essential for nurses providing family planning care?

options.A: It allows the nurse to enforce strict personal opinions on the client
options.B: It helps the nurse identify potential cultural and psychosocial barriers to contraceptive uptake
options.C: It replaces the need for informed consent
options.D: It guarantees that all clients will immediately choose permanent methods

explanation: Cultural competence enables nurses to understand a client's background, recognize underlying barriers, and tailor education without bias. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T023#GNS226_U6_T023_h2)

question: What is a frequent consequence of poor spousal communication regarding family planning?

options.A: Guaranteed permanent contraception
options.B: Covert contraceptive use and potential marital discord
options.C: Instantaneous joint decision-making
options.D: Complete elimination of gender inequality

explanation: When partners fail to communicate openly, it often leads to covert use of contraceptives, fear of conflict, and discord within the marriage. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T023#GNS226_U6_T023_h3)

question: When addressing gender dynamics in family planning, what should a nurse always prioritize?

options.A: The financial status of the husband
options.B: The safety, confidentiality, and autonomy of the client
options.C: Mandatory male partner approval for all procedures
options.D: Eliminating all cultural traditions immediately

explanation: While encouraging joint communication is ideal, the nurse must always prioritize the client's personal safety, confidentiality, and individual autonomy. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T023#GNS226_U6_T023_h3)

question: Which of the following is a core requirement for valid informed consent in contraceptive choice?

options.A: Consent must be given under pressure from family members
options.B: The client must receive comprehensive, unbiased information free from coercion
options.C: The healthcare provider must choose the method for the client
options.D: The client must sign the form without understanding potential side effects

explanation: Valid informed consent requires that the client receives full, unbiased information and makes a voluntary decision free from any coercion or pressure. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T023#GNS226_U6_T023_h4)

question: What is a violation of a client's rights within a reproductive health setting?

options.A: Pressuring a client to accept a specific contraceptive method due to provider bias
options.B: Providing information in a language the client understands
options.C: Ensuring client privacy and confidentiality
options.D: Respecting the client's right to discontinue a method

explanation: Pressuring a client to accept a method due to personal biases or targets violates their right to voluntary, uncoerced decision-making. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T023#GNS226_U6_T023_h4)

question: What is the primary purpose of utilizing frameworks like GATHER or REDI in family planning counseling?

options.A: To force the client into choosing a permanent method
options.B: To provide structured, client-centered interactions that guide choices
options.C: To replace the need for a physical nursing assessment
options.D: To speed up the clinical encounter regardless of client comprehension

explanation: Counseling frameworks provide a structured, client-centered approach that helps nurses guide clients through exploration and decision-making effectively. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T023#GNS226_U6_T023_h5)

question: Which of the following should be included in a comprehensive nursing assessment for family planning?

options.A: Only the client's current financial earnings
options.B: Reproductive goals, health status, and potential contraindications
options.C: The opinions of the client's extended family members exclusively
options.D: Mandatory blood transfusion history

explanation: A thorough nursing assessment evaluates the client's reproductive goals, medical and obstetric history, and any health factors that contraindicate certain contraceptives. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T023#GNS226_U6_T023_h5)

question: How should a nurse respond when a client expresses a common misconception, such as fear that contraceptives cause permanent infertility?

options.A: Dismiss the client's fear as foolish and ignore it
options.B: Validate the concern and provide respectful, evidence-based clarification
options.C: Refuse to provide any further care to the client
options.D: Confirm the myth to discourage contraceptive use

explanation: Nurses should validate client concerns without judgment and use evidence-based education to clarify facts and dispel myths. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T023#GNS226_U6_T023_h6)

question: Which of the following represents an operational barrier to family planning in clinical settings?

options.A: Empathetic communication by nursing staff
options.B: Stock-outs of contraceptive commodities and long waiting times
options.C: Comprehensive and clear health education
options.D: Youth-friendly clinic policies

explanation: Operational barriers include systemic challenges such as commodity stock-outs, long wait times, and unfriendly staff attitudes that discourage clients. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T023#GNS226_U6_T023_h6)

question: Which ethical principle is demonstrated when a nurse respects a client's voluntary decision to use or discontinue a contraceptive method?

options.A: Autonomy
options.B: Beneficence
options.C: Paternalism
options.D: Maleficence

explanation: Autonomy refers to the ethical principle of respecting a person's right to self-determination and independent decision-making regarding their own body. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T023#GNS226_U6_T023_h7)

question: Why is understanding local laws and the scope of practice important for nurses in family planning?

options.A: It allows nurses to make medical decisions on behalf of the client's family
options.B: It ensures legal compliance, protects client rights, and prevents professional malpractice
options.C: It removes the need to obtain informed consent from adults
options.D: It mandates that all clients use long-acting reversible contraceptives

explanation: Operating within the legal scope of practice and laws ensures that client rights are protected, ethical dilemmas are managed, and professional malpractice is avoided. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T023#GNS226_U6_T023_h7)

question: What is a primary role of the nurse during family planning follow-up appointments?

options.A: To mandate a specific contraceptive method for every client
options.B: To serve as an educator and advocate bridging clinical guidelines and client realities
options.C: To restrict access to reproductive health services
options.D: To discourage clients from asking questions about their health

explanation: Nurses act as primary educators and advocates during follow-up visits, ensuring that care aligns with the client's needs while bridging clinical guidelines and community realities. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T024#GNS226_U6_T024_h1)

question: Why is structured follow-up care particularly important in the Nigerian context?

options.A: It guarantees that clients never experience side effects
options.B: It maximizes limited clinic contacts to promote client retention and prevent unplanned pregnancies
options.C: It eliminates the need for any future medical consultations
options.D: It replaces the initial contraceptive consultation entirely

explanation: Given potential logistical challenges in accessing clinics, maximizing every follow-up contact helps retain clients and prevent unplanned pregnancies. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T024#GNS226_U6_T024_h1)

question: What is a primary objective of evaluating a contraceptive method during a follow-up visit?

options.A: To force the client to change their method immediately
options.B: To assess ongoing effectiveness, safety, and potential medical complications
options.C: To determine the client's financial income
options.D: To replace the need for physical assessments

explanation: Evaluating the method ensures it remains safe and effective while checking for any medical complications or side effects. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T024#GNS226_U6_T024_h2)

question: Why is reinforcing correct and consistent usage a key purpose of follow-up visits?

options.A: User error is a leading cause of contraceptive failure
options.B: Contraceptives never fail on their own
options.C: Clients automatically remember all instructions given at initiation
options.D: It eliminates all potential side effects

explanation: User error remains a leading cause of contraceptive failure, making reinforcement of proper usage essential during follow-up. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T024#GNS226_U6_T024_h2)

question: When is an initial early follow-up visit typically recommended after starting a new contraceptive method?

options.A: After exactly five years
options.B: Between two to six weeks
options.C: After twelve months
options.D: Only when the client becomes pregnant

explanation: Standard protocols recommend an early follow-up at two to six weeks to check initial adjustment and acute side effects. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T024#GNS226_U6_T024_h3)

question: What is a practical strategy nurses can use in Nigeria to help clients remember reinjection or follow-up dates?

options.A: Telling them to rely entirely on memory
options.B: Avoiding discussion of future appointments
options.C: Helping clients develop reminder systems like mobile alarms or calendar markings
options.D: Requiring clients to stay at the clinic permanently

explanation: Practical reminder systems like mobile phone alarms and calendar markings help clients adhere to their scheduled return dates. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T024#GNS226_U6_T024_h3)

question: What is a primary focus when assessing method compliance during a follow-up visit?

options.A: Punishing the client for missed doses
options.B: Systematically exploring barriers to correct and consistent use
options.C: Prescribing surgical procedures automatically
options.D: Ignoring whether the client is still using the method

explanation: Compliance assessment involves exploring potential barriers to adherence, such as forgetfulness or side effects, in a supportive manner. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T024#GNS226_U6_T024_h4)

question: What immediate risk does a client face if they discontinue a contraceptive method without starting an alternative?

options.A: Unintended pregnancy
options.B: Immediate permanent infertility
options.C: Severe vitamin deficiency
options.D: Mandatory hospitalization

explanation: Stopping a contraceptive method without a replacement leaves the client unprotected against an unintended pregnancy. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T024#GNS226_U6_T024_h4)

question: What is the appropriate initial nursing response when a client reports common side effects like minor spotting?

options.A: Dismiss the concerns because they are minor
options.B: Validate the experience, provide reassurance, and explain expected timelines
options.C: Immediately perform emergency surgery
options.D: Discontinue all healthcare services

explanation: Validating client experiences and providing reassurance about normal adjustment timelines helps reduce anxiety and prevents premature discontinuation. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T024#GNS226_U6_T024_h5)

question: Which of the following represents a potentially dangerous complication that nurses must screen for during follow-up?

options.A: Mild temporary fatigue
options.B: Severe visual disturbances or chest pain indicating potential thrombosis
options.C: Slight hair thinning
options.D: Mild local bruising from an injection

question: Why is screening for interval changes in health history necessary during follow-up visits?

options.A: Because medical conditions and health eligibility criteria can change over time
options.B: To update the client's home address only
options.C: Because initial screening results never change
options.D: To eliminate the need for physical examinations

explanation: Health statuses are dynamic, and new medical conditions can develop that alter a client's eligibility for certain contraceptive methods. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T024#GNS226_U6_T024_h6)

question: What guideline framework is commonly used to assess whether a new medical condition contraindicates a contraceptive method?

options.A: WHO Medical Eligibility Criteria (MEC)
options.B: National Traffic Regulations
options.C: Hospital Financial Guidelines
options.D: Standard Pharmacological Pricing Index

explanation: The WHO Medical Eligibility Criteria (MEC) provides evidence-based guidance on the safety of contraceptive methods for clients with specific medical conditions. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T024#GNS226_U6_T024_h6)

question: How should a nurse view a client's request to switch contraceptive methods?

options.A: As a failure of clinical care
options.B: As a normal part of reproductive care when needs or goals change
options.C: As a reason to deny future services
options.D: As an indication of poor personal hygiene

explanation: Method switching is a normal, expected part of reproductive care when a client's lifestyle, side effect profile, or family planning goals evolve. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T024#GNS226_U6_T024_h7)

question: What is a vital safety action when a client transitions from one contraceptive method to another?

options.A: Leaving the client without coverage for several months
options.B: Ensuring bridge coverage or immediate initiation to prevent gaps in protection
options.C: Forcing the client to choose a permanent surgical method
options.D: Discontinuing all follow-up appointments

explanation: Immediate bridge coverage or simultaneous initiation prevents any gap in protection against unintended pregnancies during the switch. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T024#GNS226_U6_T024_h7)

question: What is a primary benefit of accurate and comprehensive medical documentation in family planning?

options.A: It ensures continuity of care and allows any provider to view the client's history
options.B: It allows public sharing of client health data on social media
options.C: It replaces the need for verbal communication with the client
options.D: It guarantees that the client will never experience side effects

explanation: Comprehensive documentation ensures that all healthcare providers have access to vital history, promoting safe, continuous, and coordinated care. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T024#GNS226_U6_T024_h8)

question: Which of the following details should be explicitly recorded during a follow-up visit?

options.A: Only the client's home address and telephone number
options.B: Assessment findings, counseling provided, method status, and next return date
options.C: The personal opinions of the nurse regarding family size
options.D: Financial market trends in the local community

question: How is a family planning defaulter typically defined in clinical practice?

question: Why is managing family planning defaulters considered a priority for student nurses?

question: Which of the following is a common individual reason for a client to default on family planning?

options.A: Experiencing unmanaged side effects like weight gain or mood changes
options.B: Receiving too many follow-up phone calls from the clinic
options.C: Having excess supplies of contraceptives at home
options.D: Attending clinic appointments ahead of schedule

explanation: Unpleasant side effects that are not anticipated or properly managed are a primary driver for clients abandoning their contraceptive methods. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T025#GNS226_U6_T025_h2)

question: How do facility-level factors impact the rate of family planning defaulting?

options.A: Short waiting times encourage clients to stop visiting
options.B: Friendly healthcare workers discourage clients from returning
options.C: Stock-outs of preferred commodities and long waiting times drive clients away
options.D: Convenient clinic hours cause confusion regarding schedules

question: What is the primary facility tool used by nurses to identify clients who have missed their appointments?

options.B: Family planning registers and appointment cards
